name: Shin-Seibijo
tagline: Tokyo in 41 minutes and Shinagawa in 41 minutes. Served by 1 line.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Tokyo Monorail. Journey times to the main business districts are 46 minutes to Otemachi, 55 minutes to Shinjuku, 50 minutes to Shibuya and 41 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 5.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 8.2 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 5.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.9 m to 9.1 m, a difference of 8.2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Monorail.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Monorail. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2; for quiet, Shin-Seibijo.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Seibijo. Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 also has the Keikyu Airport Line, which Shin-Seibijo does not. With more lines, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 is 4 minutes quicker. On quiet, though, Shin-Seibijo comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Shin-Seibijo.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Shin-Seibijo in a straight line. Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 also has the Keikyu Airport Line, which Shin-Seibijo does not. With more lines, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 is 7 minutes quicker. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, though, Shin-Seibijo comes out ahead.
